pairs.subject: codegen
pairs.evidence: packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs:220 generate() builds every file in memory but then deletes the committed results/ folder and rewrites each file in place with writeFile (truncate-on-open), so an interrupted `pnpm -C packages/contract generate` leaves fewer or zero-byte committed artifacts. That is exactly the delete-then-repopulate failure generator-failure-isolation names, where the fix is a staged write and atomic swap.

techniques.evidence: packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs:220 Delete-then-repopulate of results/ followed by in-place writeFile (line 223) into src/generated; no temp-path + rename / directory swap, so an interrupt leaves a partial committed set. The cargo export (execFileSync) also has no time budget.

packages/contract/scripts/check.mjs:44 The boundary type contract sits in tier 2: committed, with a lockstep drift gate whose failure message is the regeneration command, which is the canonical case for that tier.

packages/contract/scripts/check.mjs:35 Check mode reuses the same generate() code path into a temp dir, diffs the whole generated tree (changed/missing/not-generated, so orphans and new files are covered) plus the schema, and exits 1 with the file names. Hosted in CI (see notes).

packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs:24 The generator emits a banner on every file saying it is generated, naming the generator, the source and the rebuild command (line 25). Output is deterministic (sorted names, LF normalisation), and eslint ignores **/generated/**. Gaps: no linguist-generated marker for collapsing diffs in review, and in validators.js the banner comes after @ts-nocheck/eslint-disable.

packages/contract/scripts/generate.mjs:17 This context has one generator writing one output root, so no in-context registry is needed. Whether the repo-wide generator population (tokens + contract) needs a registry is a question for a repo-level judgment.

packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs:3 Output is a pure function of the schema with no positional references into sources, so unrelated edits do not churn it; the drift check on the change is the right regime.

packages/contract/package.json:10 Regeneration is manual only. No dev, build or test door in this package (or in the consuming vite dev/build) runs generate, and no build asserts freshness. Staleness is caught only after the fact by the Rust schema_drift test and the CI check, never healed ambiently.

pairs.registryProposal: trigger-wiring assumes the pipeline can run at the consumer's dev or build door, but here the input lives in another toolchain (Rust/cargo) and the artifact is tier-2 gated. The technique should say whether, for cross-toolchain boundary contracts, a lockstep gate on the input side (a cargo test) plus the CI drift gate satisfies it, or whether a freshness stamp checked by the JS build is still required.
